S019.name: Delusions
S019.description: Fixed beliefs that do not change easily, even in the face of contradictory evidence.

subtypes.Persecutory Delusions: The false belief that one is being harmed or monitored by other people or organizations.
subtypes.Referential Delusions: The conviction that ordinary events, remarks, or behaviors have specific relevance to oneself.
subtypes.Grandiose Delusions: The false belief that one possesses special abilities, power, or fame.
subtypes.Erotomanic Delusions: The false belief that another person is in love with or has affection for them.
subtypes.Nihilistic Delusions: A destructive or negative conviction that the world is ending or that a major catastrophe will occur.
subtypes.Somatic Delusions: The baseless conviction that there is a serious abnormality with one's body or organs.
subtypes.Jealous Delusions: The conviction that one's spouse or romantic partner is being unfaithful without sufficient evidence.

S020.name: Hallucinations
S020.description: Perception-like experiences that occur without an external stimulus and are as vivid and clear as normal perception.

subtypes.Auditory Hallucinations: The perceptual experience of hearing voices or sounds when there is no actual sound.
subtypes.Visual Hallucinations: The perceptual experience of seeing people or objects that do not exist.
subtypes.Tactile Hallucinations: Experiencing the sensation of being touched or movement on the skin when there is no actual stimulus.
subtypes.Olfactory Hallucinations: The perceptual experience of smelling odors that do not exist.
subtypes.Gustatory Hallucinations: The perceptual experience of tasting flavors that are not actually present.

S022.name: Disorganized_Abnormal_Behavior
S022.description: A state where behavior and motor control are severely disturbed, appearing as movements or reactions inappropriate to the situation.

subtypes.Childlike Silliness: Inappropriate, childish, or illogical behavior appearing in situations.
subtypes.Stupor: No psychomotor activity; not actively relating to environment.
subtypes.Catalepsy: Passive induction of a posture held against gravity.
subtypes.Waxy Flexibility: Slight, even resistance to positioning by examiner.
subtypes.Mutism: No, or very little, verbal response despite the ability to speak.
subtypes.Negativism: Opposition or no response to instructions or external stimuli without apparent motive.
subtypes.Posturing: Spontaneous and active maintenance of a posture against gravity.
subtypes.Mannerism: Odd, circumstantial caricature of normal actions.
subtypes.Agitation: Excessive motor activity without obvious external cause.
subtypes.Grimacing: Contorted facial expressions irrelevant to the situation.

S023.name: Negative_Symptoms
S023.description: A state where emotions, motivation, speech, or social interest that should normally be present are diminished or lost.

subtypes.Diminished Emotional Expression: A state of reduced emotional expression in facial expressions, eye contact, intonation of speech, and movements.
subtypes.Avolition: A decrease in motivated self-initiated purposeful activities.
subtypes.Alogia: A state where the quantity of spontaneous speech is significantly reduced.
subtypes.Anhedonia: A decrease in the ability to experience pleasure or interest in enjoyable activities.
subtypes.Asociality: A state where interest in social activities or interpersonal relationships is significantly reduced.

info.persona: Corina Jones embodies a quietly curious soul who thrives on solitary rituals—sunrise beach walks, garden teas, and true‑crime podcasts—yet habitually misplaces their keys and lets a relaxed attitude toward planning sometimes turn schedules into gentle chaos.
info.professional_persona: Corina Jones is a seasoned front‑of‑house server in Hawthorne’s bustling casual‑dining scene, whose knack for memorizing menu details, casually slipping Spanish phrases into recommendations, and staying ahead of food‑safety upgrades fuels their practical curiosity as they work toward a shift‑manager role and a ServSafe Manager certification.
info.cultural_background: Corina grew up in a middle‑class, suburban family in the South Bay region of Los Angeles County. Her parents are of Anglo‑American descent, and she was raised with a blend of traditional Midwestern values—emphasis on hard work and modesty—and the relaxed, multicultural vibe of Southern California. Exposure to the diverse neighborhoods surrounding Hawthorne introduced her to Mexican and Asian cuisines, sparking her curiosity about food culture. She celebrates holidays such as Thanksgiving and Christmas, and she occasionally joins local community festivals like the Fourth‑of‑July beach fireworks. Although primarily English‑speaking, she picked up conversational Spanish through community interactions, reflecting the linguistic tapestry of her home region.
info.hobbies_and_interests: In her off‑hours, Corina seeks solitary, low‑stimulus activities that recharge her. She devotes time to reading contemporary fiction and poetry, often curled up with a cup of tea in her garden. Gardening itself is a favorite pursuit; she tends to herbs and succulents, experimenting with small batch preserves. Baking simple breads and pastries lets her apply her culinary curiosity without the pressure of a fast‑paced kitchen. She also enjoys long, solitary walks along the nearby beach at sunrise, capturing subtle moments through a compact digital camera. Listening to true‑crime podcasts and journaling about daily observations are regular habits that satisfy her inquisitive nature while preserving her need for quiet.
info.sports_persona: Corina Jones finds fitness in solitary sunrise beach walks along the Pacific and a weekly yoga session, while they cheer the LA Galaxy and the Los Angeles Lakers on game nights and casually join a community beach‑volleyball circle when a calm evening invites a gentle rally.
info.arts_persona: Corina Jones spends evenings lost in contemporary fiction by Ocean Vuong and the poetry of Mary Oliver, enjoys true‑crime podcasts like 'Serial' and 'My Favorite Murder', and they unwind to the mellow piano of Norah Jones and the indie folk of Damien Rice, allowing these artistic flavors to colour their solitary reflections.
info.travel_persona: Corina Jones prefers low‑key getaways that promise solitude, such as sunrise hikes in Joshua Tree, a weekend of garden inspiration in Kyoto's tea houses, and a relaxed road‑trip along California’s Pacific Coast Highway, planning trips with a flexible itinerary that respects both a modest budget and their love for quiet corners.
info.culinary_persona: Corina Jones delights in baking simple sourdough loaves and lemon shortbread while tending a herb garden of rosemary, thyme, and basil, often flavoring preserves with cilantro‑lime zest and kimchi‑inspired spice blends, and they savor Mexican‑inspired tacos al pastor and Asian‑style miso ramen for inspiration.

info.persona: Michael Gascon, a diligent security strategist with a poet’s soul, balances careful risk‑assessment with spontaneous acoustic songwriting, habitually worries about hidden threats, yet they find calm in sunrise hikes and daily meditation.
info.professional_persona: Michael Gascon, a 45‑year‑old security professional certified in first aid, CPR, and incident reporting, merges their humanities‑rooted analytical mindset with hands‑on protective‑service expertise to craft thorough threat‑assessment protocols, and they are known for balancing meticulous planning with a compassionate, community‑focused leadership style that often worries about unseen vulnerabilities.
info.cultural_background: Michael was raised in a middle‑class, predominantly white community in Utah, with family roots that blend Anglo‑American and Hispanic (or French) ancestry hinted by his surname, Gascon. His upbringing was influenced by the values of the local LDS‑shaped culture—emphasizing service, modesty, and community cohesion—though he pursued a secular academic path in the humanities. This background gives him an appreciation for both traditional American work ethic and a broader, multicultural perspective gained through his education. Living in Orem, he participates in the region’s blend of suburban family life, outdoor recreation, and a close‑knit community ethos.
info.hobbies_and_interests: In his free time, Michael enjoys exploring the Wasatch foothills on hikes, which provide both physical activity and a calming connection to nature. He is an avid reader of historical biographies and philosophical works, feeding his curiosity while offering practical insights. Music is a creative outlet; he plays acoustic guitar and writes song lyrics. Michael volunteers at a local community center, running workshops on conflict resolution for at‑risk youth. He experiments with cooking healthy meals, often using fresh, locally sourced ingredients. To manage stress, he practices mindfulness meditation, attends occasional yoga classes, and captures landscapes and candid street scenes through photography.
info.sports_persona: Michael Gascon, an avid outdoor enthusiast, spends weekends hiking the Wasatch foothills with the Wasatch Trail Runners, plays pickup basketball while cheering for the Utah Jazz, trains at a local CrossFit box, coaches a youth soccer team, and they also volunteer as a safety trainer for the league, balancing their love of nature with a competitive, team‑oriented spirit.
info.arts_persona: Michael Gascon, a dedicated acoustic guitarist and lyricist, draws lyrical inspiration from Joni Mitchell and Leonard Cohen, attends Utah Symphony concerts, captures candid street scenes with their Nikon D850, and curates a personal photo blog where they showcase both musical and visual storytelling.
info.travel_persona: Michael Gascon, a meticulous traveler, has hiked the Grand Canyon, biked the Pacific Coast Highway, and dreams of photographing Patagonia’s Torres del Paine, and they prefer carefully planned road trips that blend adventure with budget‑friendly stays at family‑run B&Bs.
info.culinary_persona: Michael Gascon, a health‑focused home cook, frequently prepares quinoa bowls with roasted root vegetables, wild salmon with almond‑pesto, and heirloom tomato salads topped with fresh basil, but they have a habit of over‑seasoning with sea salt, turning even simple dishes into bold flavor experiments.

info.persona: Kathy Lacaze blends Midwestern community spirit, a competitive curiosity, and a love for arts‑infused education, balancing disciplined planning with occasional spontaneous indulgences, all while navigating the health quirks of midlife.
info.professional_persona: Kathy Lacaze is a veteran secondary school teacher who designs interdisciplinary curricula weaving art, literature, and critical thinking, and leverages her strong classroom management, tech integration, and mentorship skills to champion a collaborative, project‑based learning culture while eyeing a future as a department chair or district curriculum coordinator.
info.cultural_background: Kathy hails from a multi‑generational Midwestern white family with Irish and German roots, raised in small‑town Indiana. Her upbringing reflects classic Midwestern values of community, hard work, and modesty, and she maintains strong ties to local traditions such as county fairs, church gatherings, and seasonal celebrations. While she embraces the broader American cultural landscape, her appreciation for the arts is shaped by both her personal curiosity and the regional support for community arts programs, which she integrates into her teaching and volunteer work.
info.hobbies_and_interests: Outside of school, Kathy is an avid supporter of the arts and community life. She enjoys visiting local galleries and museums, participating in a community theater group, painting with friends, and attending live music performances. She is a dedicated member of a weekly book club, loves hiking the trails of nearby nature preserves, and often organizes potluck gatherings for her neighborhood. Her love of culinary experiments and gardening also provides creative outlets, and she frequently volunteers at the town’s annual art fair.
info.sports_persona: Kathy Lacaze is a devoted fan of the Indianapolis Colts and Indiana Pacers, plays in a community tennis league on Saturdays, joins a local hiking club for seasonal trail outings, and volunteers as a coach for the high‑school girls’ cross‑country team.
info.arts_persona: Kathy Lacaze immerses herself in the regional arts scene by acting in the town’s community theater, painting with a weekly friends’ group, curating visits to the Indianapolis Museum of Art and local galleries featuring artists like Grant Wood and contemporary painter Jane Smith, and organizing the annual art fair that showcases local talent.
info.travel_persona: Kathy Lacaze prefers organized road‑trip itineraries that blend cultural stops—such as a weekend in Charleston, a beer festival in Cincinnati, and a heritage tour of a European village— with nature hikes in Shenandoah and Hocking Hills, always budgeting through a travel rewards credit card and planning trips around the school calendar.
info.culinary_persona: Kathy Lacaze has an intermediate cooking skill level, delights in garden‑to‑table dishes like roasted beet salad with goat cheese, butternut squash ravioli, and homemade apple‑cinnamon pie, frequently experiments with German sauerkraut and Irish soda bread recipes, and hosts potluck dinners featuring farm‑fresh vegetables and locally sourced cheese.
